post_title: What will the Northern Sierra 8-Station Precipitation Index be for November 26, 2026 (water-year-to-date, inches)?

question.title: What will the Northern Sierra 8-Station Precipitation Index be for November 26, 2026 (water-year-to-date, inches)?
question.description:
The Northern Sierra 8-Station Precipitation Index (8SI) is the average of precipitation at eight northern Sierra Nevada stations (Mount Shasta City, Shasta Dam, Mineral, Quincy, Brush Creek, Sierraville RS, Blue Canyon and Pacific House), accumulated from October 1, the start of California's water year. DWR uses it, alongside the San Joaquin 5-Station and Tulare Basin 6-Station indices, as a headline indicator of Sierra wetness in water-supply forecasting (including Bulletin 120). The 1991-2020 average for a full water year is 53.2 inches; the wettest water year on record (2016-17) reached 94.7 inches and the driest (1923-24) 17.1 inches.

As of November 13, 2026 the index stands at 0.72 inches water-year-to-date, roughly 14% of the 1991-2020 average for the date — an exceptionally dry start after a mostly dry October (about 0.46 in had accumulated by October 23, and about 0.7 in by November 4). For scale, recent November monthly totals for the index were 13.49 in (Nov 2024) and 7.72 in (Nov 2025), and typical accumulation is roughly 5 inches by mid-November.

The question hinges on a storm sequence now arriving. NWS Sacramento and local forecasts call for the season's first prolonged stormy stretch beginning Friday November 13 (1-3 inches of liquid in the mountains Friday-Saturday, with a second system Sunday night into Monday), with more Pacific storms behind it through late November. Weather West (Daniel Swain, Nov 11) described three to four successive winter-like storms over roughly nine days, with 14-day rainfall accumulations across much of California generally exceeding average totals for the entire month of November; the CPC outlook favours above-average precipitation over much of California for November 21 - December 4, and reporting on Nov 12-13 described the season's first atmospheric-river sequence and 50-foot surf. Snowfall at these stations counts as precipitation in the gauge record, so cold storms do not by themselves reduce the index.

Data source: CDEC station 8SI (https://cdec.water.ca.gov/dynamicapp/QueryDaily?s=8SI) publishes daily incremental precipitation ('PPT INC') and the water-year cumulative value ('RAIN') in inches, labelled by calendar date and marked provisional; a fixed 31-day window can be requested with an end-date parameter. The index is also plotted against historical years in CDEC's 8-Station Index chart (https://cdec.water.ca.gov/reportapp/javareports?name=PLOT_ESI.pdf).

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the water-year-to-date value of the Northern Sierra 8-Station Precipitation Index (CDEC station code 8SI) for the observation date 2026-11-26 — i.e. the value in the cumulative 'RAIN' column (inches) on the row dated 11/26/2026 in the daily data table at https://cdec.water.ca.gov/dynamicapp/QueryDaily?end=2026-11-26&s=8SI (for example, a row showing RAIN = 5.83 resolves as 5.83). The first value CDEC publishes for that date is used, and later revisions of CDEC's provisional data do not change the resolution. If no value for 11/26/2026 has been published when resolution is attempted on November 27, 2026, resolution waits until CDEC publishes it; if CDEC never publishes a value for that date, the question is annulled. If the CDEC page is inaccessible, the value may be taken from CDEC's daily precipitation report at http://cdec.water.ca.gov/reportapp/javareports?name=DailyPrecip (the 8SI value carrying data date 11/26/2026) or otherwise from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
question.fine_print: CDEC's date label for each daily precipitation value is used as-is, regardless of the exact hourly cut-off or timezone convention behind that label; precipitation recorded after that observation does not affect the answer. The index is a DWR composite and is not recomputed from the eight individual station records by the resolver. Because CDEC re-renders its pages with current data, resolvers should preserve a copy of the page used (e.g. a Wayback Machine capture) at the time of resolution.
